title: Verifier-Gated Dynamic Task Decomposition for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
research_question: Can a verifier-gated orchestration policy that adaptively decides when to decompose, merge, or re-route subtasks reduce error propagation and coordination overhead compared with static multi-agent task decomposition pipelines?
hypothesis: Static decomposition and fixed escalation policies are a weak point in multi-agent workflows because they either over-decompose easy tasks or under-scrutinize hard ones; adding lightweight verifier signals to gate decomposition and handoffs will improve task success per token and per latency budget.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejection of ideas centered on uncertainty averaging and generic adaptive escalation for agent orchestration, suggesting that those angles are already explored or insufficiently novel. At the same time, the self-adaptive systems entry highlights a broader unresolved issue: runtime decisions should not rely on a single fixed model when multiple plausible scenarios may explain observed failures. This creates a concrete gap for agentic workflows: current orchestration ideas appear to focus on averaging risk or escalation, but not on using runtime verifier evidence to control the granularity of decomposition itself. A verifier-gated decomposition policy targets a high-value bottleneck in agent collaboration—error propagation through unnecessary handoffs—while staying distinct from previously rejected uncertainty-averaging proposals.
